sorMethod.method: Estimated Strength of Record; lower benchmark match-or-exceed probability ranks better
sorMethod.benchmark: Mean full-precision SRS of the top 25 FBS teams; shared across every schedule
sorMethod.validation_caveat: Final-season SRS is used throughout; fit diagnostics are not independent predictive validation.
sorMethod.assumptions: Independent games; fixed team strength; actual played schedules including repeats and synthetic FCS opponents. Synthetic buckets are not ranked. Ties rejected. Zero wins gives probability 1. Competition ranks compare probabilities rounded to 12 decimals.

effMethod.model: points scored = mu + offence + defence + home field
effMethod.home_field_source: Taken from the ratings export, not re-estimated, so this decomposition and the published SRS rest on the same figure.
effMethod.solver: Alternating least squares (Gauss-Seidel on the normal equations), offence and defence recentred on zero each sweep
effMethod.pace: Per game, not per drive. No national screen carries punts or field-goal attempts, so a league-wide drive count cannot be built from the source set. Football drives also vary far less than basketball possessions: the three dynasty schools run 10.4 to 11.8 a game.

sosMethod.method: Mean opponent SRS per scheduled game
sosMethod.opponents: Includes synthetic FCS buckets using their calculated SRS; repeated opponents count once per game.

coverage.results: 842 regular-season games, weeks 0–14, across 138 real teams plus five synthetic FCS buckets. All 138 real teams have exactly 12 games. Conference championships and Central Michigan–Tennessee are excluded from ratings and season totals.

summaries.title: Western Michigan · 11–1
summaries.text: Western won its first seven games and finished the regular season 11–1, scoring 380 points and allowing 193. Its only loss came against Central Michigan; four straight wins afterward included a season-ending shutout of Kent State. The Broncos did it against a schedule of close to average difficulty, 76th of 138, so a 15.6-point scoring margin carries through to the 18th-strongest opponent-adjusted rating in the country. Western went on to lose the conference championship game to Central Michigan and won its bowl.

summaries.title: Eastern Michigan · 4–8
summaries.text: Eastern opened 2–0 but finished 4–8, with seven losses decided by eight points or fewer. The Eagles scored 202 points and allowed 227, pairing wins over Buffalo and Akron with a difficult finish against Central Michigan. Their schedule rated 75th of 138, almost exactly average, so the narrow scoring deficit is not a product of the opposition: it leaves Eastern 79th in opponent-adjusted terms. Eastern did not reach a bowl.

summaries.title: Central Michigan · 11–1
summaries.text: Central closed the regular season with ten straight wins and swept both Michigan rivals. The Chippewas scored 396 points and allowed just 142, the strongest scoring margin of the three programs. They also drew the hardest schedule of the three, 71st of 138 and the only one above the national average, which lifts their opponent-adjusted rating to sixth nationally. Central then won the conference championship and reached the College Football Playoff, losing to Tennessee in the first round.
